newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nedlloyd sees 1997 as transition year.
newsitem.headline: Nedlloyd sees 1997 as transition year.

text.p: Dutch shipping and road transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV said on Thursday 1997 would be a transition year and gave no forecast as to future results.
"We make no statement on the outlook. It is too early in the year. It is also too early in the merger process. 1997 is a transition year," group chairman Leo Berndsen told a news conference.
"In May, we should be able to give a forecast," he added.

Berndsen said Nedlloyd was still on line to produce a return on capital of 10 percent. However, he declined to say when that target would be reached. In 1996, the return was between three and four percent, he said.
This year will be one of transition because of the recently concluded merger between the container businesses of Nedlloyd and Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company .
Nedlloyd added that the uncertainty of shipping tariffs, and their likely erosion, made profit for the P&O Nedlloyd joint venture predictions hard to make.
However, the company said its merger would make it one of the strongest in the ocean shipping industry.
"The platform is ready and it is encouraging for the future. We can manage our cost savings and we will sit much better with them," said Paul Bijvoets, executive board member of P&O Nedlloyd.
He said the cost reduction target of $200 million within 18 months was still on track.

The company added that P&O Nedlloyd would decide by the middle of the year to which of two competing shipping consortia it wishes to ally itself. Nedlloyd belongs to the Global Alliance, P&O Containers to the Grand Alliance.
